weather.tip: An 80% chance of rain on Deepavali day means wet roads just when everyone heads out; if you are driving towards the airport road, remember it is down to one lane at the elevated corridor work, so leave earlier than the app suggests.

edge.title: The loan that needs a fee first
edge.setup: A call or WhatsApp message: your government-scheme loan for a small business has been approved, you just need to pay a processing, insurance or 'file release' charge today. The amount is small next to the loan. An agent with official-looking papers is warm and patient.
edge.tell: A lender asking for money before any money reaches you.
move: Hang up and walk into the bank branch, or open the scheme's official portal yourself, to ask whether any loan in your name exists.
Never pay a private agent or personal UPI ID to 'release' or 'insure' a sanctioned loan; real charges are deducted by the lender from the loan and shown in the sanction letter.
If you have already paid, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in at once, and tell your bank.
edge.why: The fee is the whole product: the loan was never real. Hope for a large sum makes a smaller upfront payment feel like a toll, and each 'one more charge' that follows is cheaper to pay than to admit the first was a mistake. A sunk payment is the scammer's best leverage.
edge.variants: Same shape: lottery 'tax' before the prize, a job fee before the joining letter, 'GST clearance' on a courier or inheritance.

lens.name: Planning fallacy
lens.one_line: We estimate time and cost from the best-case plan, so projects almost always run late and over budget.
lens.detail: People picture the plan going smoothly and forget the delays that hit every real project: approvals, weather, supply, rework. Asking 'how long did similar projects actually take?' gives a far better estimate than asking 'how long should this take?'. It is the base rate applied to schedules.
elsewhere: Home renovations finishing weeks after the contractor's date.
Your own 'it will take ten minutes' tasks.
lens.test: What did the last three similar things actually take, and why would this one be different?
lens.today: Bengaluru Traffic Police and BDA have set an 18-month window for the elevated corridor work on the airport road, and The Times of India notes motorists already doubt the deadline will hold while the suggested alternative routes jam up. The test above applies directly: ask how long comparable road and Metro projects here have actually run, and plan your airport and Hebbal trips for the longer answer rather than the announced one.

moved.what: Only one lane of KIA Road will be blocked for the BDA elevated corridor project, and BDA says there is no complete closure of Ballari Road during the 18 months of work (Times of India, The Hindu).
moved.so_what: The road stays open but slower; for flights, add buffer to your usual drive time, and do not assume the alternative routes are clear, since Times of India reports they are already jammed.

moved.what: Karnataka's chief electoral officer has admitted lapses in the SIR electoral roll revision, with duplicate IDs found (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Check that your own name and details appear correctly and once on the electoral roll while the revision is under way; a duplicate or missing entry is easier to fix now than at election time.

moved.what: A Bengaluru eye hospital has reported its first firecracker injury before Deepavali (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you light anything today, keep a bucket of water nearby and never lean over a lit cracker; if something hits the eye, go straight to a hospital rather than waiting to see if it settles.

moved.what: Dalal Street opens for a one-hour Muhurat trading session on Deepavali, and the Times of India has run a 'stocks to buy for Samvat 2083' list.
moved.so_what: The session is ceremonial; treat a festival stock list as someone's opinion, not a reason to move money today.

moved.what: A Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight returned to Bengaluru after a threat note was found in a toilet (The Hindu, NDTV, India Today).
moved.so_what: If you fly today or tomorrow, check flight status before leaving home and keep a plan B for a delay, since a security return can cascade through the day's schedule.

carry_over.prompt: An auto driver refuses the meter and quotes a flat fare double the usual on a rainy festival evening, and there is no other auto in sight; what is your test?
carry_over.answer: If you're arguing about the price, you've already accepted that he's the only option.
